text:
nina: Quick sync — proposing a 'soft-failover' flow: edge router can switch requests to a warm backup model when rolling canary sees latency p95 > 200ms OR 5% error rate for two consecutive windows. Router keeps session affinity for N tokens, then TTL expires. Thoughts?

samir: I like soft-failover. Two Qs: how do we define 'warm backup'? same model quantized? smaller model? and who owns the decision surface — router or rollout controller?

liz: Prefer controller owns policy. Router should be simple: expose signals (latency/errors/health) and act on a verdict from controller with TTL. Otherwise we duplicate policy code.

nina: Reasonable. Controllers send short signed 'fallback token' with reason + expiry; router validates and applies. Keeping logic central lets us A/B policy easy.

kevin: Concern: latency of controller call adds path. We should allow local fast-fail rules (simple thresholds) as emergency path. Controller verdict preferred but not required.

samir: Agree. Local circuit-breaker for immediate fallback, with subsequent reconciliation from controller. Also: cache priming — when we failover to smaller model we need to prime KV cache to avoid cold penalty.

ada: On the priming: controller can request a warmup trace to the backup before routing traffic. That implies warmup API: /warmup?variant=small&keys=[...]. Who implements?

nina: Infra owns warmup API. It must accept opaque keys and replay a short prefix. Thermal test needed to avoid overloading clusters.

ops-bot: Note: add telemetry flag 'fallback_reason' and 'fallback_source' (local/controller) to traces. Also track success_rate post-fallback.

liz: Policy API shape proposal: POST /v1/fallback-eval {route, recent_metrics, session_id} -> {action: none|fallback:variant, ttl, reason}. Controller keeps decision history for audits.

kevin: Edge-case: multi-variant sessions (user on model A but cached tokens on model B). We need a path to forward-decode or rebase KV cache. Probably too complex — maybe we prefer stateless fallback for first N tokens.

samir: We should document expected user-visible impact (e.g., short hallucination risk) and ensure rollback path: automatic revert after X minutes if metrics stable.

nina: Action items: 1) draft RFC with API contract + signed token proto. 2) infra spike for warmup API and controller stub. 3) telemetry schema. I'll own RFC. Anyone volunteer to spike warmup?

kevin: I'll do the warmup spike next sprint.

ada: :thumbsup:

liz: :raised_hands: I'll sketch policy API.

ops-bot: Reminder: create incident hunt playbook entry for fallback-induced quality regressions.

samir: Cool. Let's sync tomorrow 10am. nina, can you drop RFC link in channel when ready?

nina: Will do. Thanks all.
